biggest_catch: There is a $0 annual fee, so the math is clean — but this is not a flat signup payment. Discover matches the cash back you earn in your first year, so if you barely use the card you get barely anything; the 'bonus' is entirely driven by how much cash back you generate from approval through your first 365 days.
catches: Only pursue spending you already planned to do — never overspend just to chase a bonus; buying things to hit a threshold wipes out the bonus math and is how people lose money on this.
Only new Discover cardholders qualify, and your account must remain open through the match period — closing or losing the account kills the match.
The match is added within two billing periods after the end of your first 365 days, so you wait up to a year plus two billing cycles to see it.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily dip your credit score by a few points.
The card's variable APR (around 20%+) will erase the entire bonus in a month or two if you carry a balance — pay the full statement balance every month.
